title: VisualIntent
description:
The single structured representation that EVERY input mode (text, image, video, reference card, preset, recipe) converts into - identity pillar 2. Exactly the 20 keys the brief fixes: 19 array-valued visual categories plus the per-category `confidence` map. No more keys, no fewer; all 20 are REQUIRED and arrays may be empty, so every consumer can index any category without a null check.

ARRAY ELEMENT TYPE (canonical decision): each element is an IntentChip OBJECT, not a bare string. Bare strings make the product impossible: Selective Inheritance needs to know WHICH reference contributed a value (ref_id), the conflict UI needs to show two competing values with their sources side by side, 'AI output is a proposal, never a commitment' needs per-chip confidence and per-chip lock/edit, and video provenance needs a timespan. A bare string carries none of that, so a string-typed intent would collapse the product into the prompt builder the brief forbids.

COMPACT FORM: $defs/compact is the interop/export profile where every element is a bare taxonomy id. It is lossless with respect to the SEMANTIC PAYLOAD (the exact set of taxonomy ids per category, which is all a generation prompt depends on) and lossy only with respect to provenance metadata (source, ref_id, confidence, lock, evidence). Round-trip guarantee: compact -> normalizeVisualIntent -> compactVisualIntent returns the identical document.

NORMALIZE CONTRACT - normalizeVisualIntent(input, ctx) -> VisualIntent (full):
  input : anything matching $defs/ingest (partial, compact, full, or mixed)
  ctx   : { taxonomy, default_source='user', default_ref_id=null, now, locale }
  1. Fill every missing key of the 20 with [] (confidence with {}).
  2. String element s -> { value:s, label: taxonomy[s].label ?? humanize(s), source: ctx.default_source, confidence: (source==='user' ? 1.0 : 0.5), locked:false }.
  3. Object element -> fill label from taxonomy, confidence default as in (2), locked default false, custom default false.
  4. Rewrite deprecated ids to replaced_by and append {from,to} to the returned rewrites log.
  5. Move any props.* value found outside `scene` into `scene` with origin_category='props'.
  6. Deduplicate by (category, value): keep max confidence, union contributors[], OR the locked flags, keep the earliest created_at. Duplicates are AGREEMENT, never conflict.
  7. Sort each array by (order asc, confidence desc, value asc) for stable diffing.
  8. Recompute confidence[c] via aggConfidence unless the caller passed keep_confidence=true.
  Idempotent: normalize(normalize(x)) deep-equals normalize(x). Total: it never throws on a valid ingest document; unknown taxonomy ids become custom:true chips rather than errors.

VisualIntent carries no schema_version of its own because that would be a 21st key. It is a VALUE OBJECT, always embedded in a versioned container (ExplorerState, VisualRecipe, history entry) - or wrapped in $defs/document when it must be persisted or exported standalone.

weather.description: Dominant meteorological condition (sunny, overcast, rain, snow). SINGLE-DOMINANT for the dominant condition; secondary atmospherics (weather.fog, weather.mist, weather.haze) are modifier nodes with exclusivity_group=null so 'rain + fog' never registers as a conflict.

confidence.description: PER-CATEGORY AGGREGATE confidence, category -> [0,1]. Per-VALUE confidence lives on each chip (IntentChip.confidence); this map answers 'how well do we believe this category is characterised at all', which is what the UI needs to grey out or flag a whole chip row. Default aggregation aggConfidence(c): 1.0 if any chip in c has locked=true or source='user'; otherwise max(chip.confidence) over the category, rounded to 3 decimals; absent (or 0) when the category array is empty. It is a STORED ADVISORY CACHE: writers may override it, readers must recompute after any chip edit.

chip_source.description: Provenance of a chip. Answers 'who put this here', which the per-chip provenance UI renders and which precedence rules read.

oneOf.title: user
oneOf.description: Typed, picked from browse, or hand-edited by the person. Highest precedence; never overwritten by a mix.

oneOf.title: analyzer_image
oneOf.description: Produced by the image analyzer adapter over a still. Forbidden in camera_motion; capped at 0.6 with evidence.kind='implied' in motion.

oneOf.title: analyzer_video
oneOf.description: Produced by the video analyzer adapter. The only source allowed to author camera_motion, and the only one that can carry a t_start_s/t_end_s timespan.

oneOf.title: analyzer_text
oneOf.description: Produced by parsing/expanding a free-text query into taxonomy ids.

oneOf.title: reference
oneOf.description: Inherited from a Reference's stored visual_attributes through a ReferenceMix (Selective Inheritance). ref_id is REQUIRED.

oneOf.title: preset
oneOf.description: Came from a saved preset in data/presets.json.

oneOf.title: query_expansion
oneOf.description: Added automatically by alias/related-hop expansion of the user's query. Always low confidence and always removable in one click.

oneOf.title: mix_resolution
oneOf.description: Materialised by a user resolving a conflict (choosing a dominant reference). ref_id is REQUIRED and points at the winner.

oneOf.title: inferred
oneOf.description: Derived by a deterministic rule with no model involved (e.g. framing.close_up implies camera_distance.near). Never above 0.5 confidence.

evidence.description: Where a chip came from inside the medium. This is what lets a video reference say 'the dolly-in happens between 1.2s and 3.4s' - an image reference structurally cannot fill the temporal fields.

kind.description: observed = directly visible/measurable; implied = inferred from a static cue such as motion blur; stated = asserted by the user or by source metadata; derived = produced by a deterministic rule.

bbox.description: [x, y, w, h] normalised to 0..1 in the source frame.

t_start_s.description: VIDEO ONLY. Start of the interval evidencing this chip.

t_end_s.description: VIDEO ONLY. End of the interval. MUST be >= t_start_s.

keyframe_url.description: Thumbnail/keyframe URL used as the chip's visual proof. Never a data: URI of full media - binaries are never stored.

detector.description: Adapter instance id that produced the evidence (e.g. 'analyzer-adapter:local@2'), NOT a hardcoded model name.

intent_chip.title: IntentChip
intent_chip.description: One value inside one VisualIntent category. Rendered by src/ui/intent-chips.js.

id.description: Optional stable instance id (chip_...). Required only when the chip must be addressed across undo/redo or across a conflict record.

value.description: A taxonomy id (default) or free text when custom=true.

label.description: Display text. Derived from taxonomy[value].label when absent; user-editable without changing value. Lens example: value 'lens.35mm_like' -> label '35mm-like perspective'.

confidence.description: Per-VALUE confidence in [0,1]. Defaults: 1.0 for source='user', 0.5 for analyzer/expansion sources when the adapter reports nothing.

ref_id.description: The reference this chip was inherited from. REQUIRED when source is 'reference' or 'mix_resolution'.

locked.description: User pinned this value: applyMix, re-analysis and query expansion MUST NOT remove, replace or re-rank it. A locked chip still participates in conflict DISPLAY.

origin_category.description: The category this chip semantically belongs to when it differs from the array it is stored in. Only legal use today: props.* chips stored in `scene`. Keeps Reference <-> intent round-trips lossless.

custom.description: True when value is free text outside the taxonomy. Custom chips are never used for structured metadata matching; they still reach the prompt and the keyword index.

negate.description: Exclusion. A chip with negate=true routes to the StructuredPrompt `constraints` slot regardless of its category, emitting negative_fragment (or 'no <prompt_fragment>').

order.description: Explicit ordering within the category. Primary use: an ordered camera_motion sequence ('dolly in, then pan left' = two chips, order 0 and 1, disjoint evidence timespans).

weight.description: Emphasis hint for formatters that support weighting. Never affects conflict detection.

alternatives.description: Runner-up values the analyzer considered. Powers the 'proposal, not commitment' swap menu.

contributors.description: Every reference that contributed this same value. Two references agreeing is AGREEMENT, not conflict; the UI shows '2 references agree'.

contested.description: DERIVED CACHE. True when this chip participates in an open conflict in the active ReferenceMix. MUST be recomputed on load; never trusted from storage.

allOf.$comment: INV-INT-3: an inherited chip must name its source reference.
INV-INT-4: deterministic inference is never presented as strong evidence.

compact.title: VisualIntentCompact
compact.description: Interop/export profile: every element is a bare taxonomy id string. Same 20 required keys. Lossless for the semantic payload, lossy for provenance. Produced by compactVisualIntent(full) = { c: unique(chips.map(ch => ch.value)).filter(v => !ch.custom && !ch.negate) }; custom and negated chips are dropped with a warning because they have no taxonomy id to carry.

ingest.title: VisualIntentIngest
ingest.description: The permissive wire shape accepted by normalizeVisualIntent: any subset of the 20 keys, elements may be bare ids, chips, or a mix. NEVER persist this shape.

document.title: VisualIntentDocument
document.description: Envelope for persisting or exporting a standalone VisualIntent. Exists so VisualIntent itself can stay at exactly 20 keys while every PERSISTED object still carries schema_version.

intent.description: Either profile; `form` is the discriminator and the allOf below pins it. anyOf (not oneOf) because a sparsely-populated intent can legitimately satisfy both profiles.
